columns.Description: Divergent water-holding (drip-loss) phenotypes in porcine centrifugal drip (longissimus thoracis et lumborum) across postmortem aging days 1/3/7 (di Luca et al. 2016, *PLOS ONE*); the identified protein/fragment-spot table (59 unique proteins with UniProt IDs) is available as open Supporting Information ([S1 Table](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0150605.s002)); the paper's original UCD-2DPAGE database deposit is no longer reachable

inventory.name: TMT-based quantitative proteomic analysis of porcine muscle associated with postmortem meat quality

columns.Study: TMT-based quantitative proteomic analysis of porcine muscle associated with postmortem meat quality
columns.Description: High- vs low-quality porcine longissimus (4 vs 4) postmortem (Hou et al. 2020, *Food Chemistry*); full ~1011-protein quantification table, 140 differentially expressed proteins, and GO/KEGG enrichment in Supplementary Tables S1–S3 — supplementary data, not a repository deposit

inventory.name: snRNA-Seq and spatial transcriptome reveal cell-cell crosstalk mediated metabolic regulation in porcine skeletal muscle

columns.Study: snRNA-Seq and spatial transcriptome reveal cell-cell crosstalk mediated metabolic regulation in porcine skeletal muscle
columns.Description: Single-nucleus RNA-seq plus spatial transcriptome of porcine skeletal muscle mapping cell-cell crosstalk that mediates metabolic regulation; the data-availability statement places raw sequence data in ScienceDB with no accession named, and states evaluation data are in the paper and Supporting Information

inventory.name: Pig genome functional annotation enhances the biological interpretation of complex traits and human disease

columns.Study: Pig genome functional annotation enhances the biological interpretation of complex traits and human disease
columns.Description: Pig functional-genome annotation across tissues (regulatory elements, chromatin states) enhancing interpretation of complex traits; eight-tissue data at GEO GSE158430, six gut tissues at ENA [`PRJEB37735`](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJEB37735), RRBS methylomes at ENA [`PRJNA762083`](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/?term=PRJNA762083), all also on the FAANG data portal

inventory.name: Profiling of open chromatin in developing pig (Sus scrofa) muscle to identify regulatory regions

columns.Study: Profiling of open chromatin in developing pig (Sus scrofa) muscle to identify regulatory regions
columns.Description: Open-chromatin (ATAC-seq, n=24) and matched RNA-seq (n=26) of developing pig muscle in large- vs small-sized day-90 fetal piglets to identify muscle regulatory regions; ATAC-seq at ENA PRJEB41485, RNA-seq at ENA [`PRJEB41488`](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJEB41488)

inventory.name: Tecator NIR meat spectra (Infratec Food and Feed Analyzer benchmark)

columns.Study: Tecator NIR meat spectra (Infratec Food and Feed Analyzer benchmark)
columns.Description: Classic NIR spectroscopy regression benchmark: 100-channel near-infrared absorbance spectra of finely chopped pure-meat samples with lab-measured fat, moisture, and protein, recorded on a Tecator Infratec analyzer; a compact public-domain testbed for spectral fat/moisture/protein prediction relevant to cultivated-pork composition QC

inventory.name: ATAC-Seq and scRNA-Seq for sheep hypoxia acclimatization

columns.Study: ATAC-Seq and scRNA-Seq for sheep hypoxia acclimatization
columns.Description: Sheep high-altitude hypoxia-acclimatization multi-omics resource; time-resolved bulk RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq from multiple tissues in a plain-to-plateau transplant model — an ovine chromatin-accessibility and single-cell deposit

inventory.name: Proteomics analysis to investigate the effect of oxidized protein on meat color and water holding capacity in Tan mutton under low temperature storage

columns.Study: Proteomics analysis to investigate the effect of oxidized protein on meat color and water holding capacity in Tan mutton under low temperature storage
columns.Description: Tan mutton under −2/−4/−18 °C storage versus fresh control (Tao et al. 2021, *LWT*); full list of 1,089 proteins with differentially changed oxidation sites in Supplementary Table 1 — supplementary data, not a repository deposit

inventory.name: Proteomic investigation of protein profile changes and amino acid residue-level modification in cooked lamb longissimus thoracis et lumborum: the effect of roasting

columns.Study: Proteomic investigation of protein profile changes and amino acid residue-level modification in cooked lamb longissimus thoracis et lumborum: the effect of roasting
columns.Description: Lamb LTL roasted 0/5/10 min (Yu et al. 2016, *Meat Science*); full per-run protein-identification reports and annotated MS/MS spectra of heat-modified peptides in Supplementary data 2–3 — supplementary data, not a repository deposit

inventory.name: A hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HILIC-MS) based metabolomics study on colour stability of ovine meat

columns.Study: A hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HILIC-MS) based metabolomics study on colour stability of ovine meat
columns.Description: Colour-stable versus colour-labile ovine loin (longissimus) under MAP/VAC packaging (Subbaraj et al. 2016, *Meat Science*); full detected-metabolite table (m/z, retention time, ionisation mode, confidence level, fold-change) in Supplementary Table S1 — supplementary data, not a repository deposit

inventory.name: Proteomic and metabolomic analysis reveals candidate biomarkers and meat quality differences in divergent climatically adapted sheep breeds

columns.Study: Proteomic and metabolomic analysis reveals candidate biomarkers and meat quality differences in divergent climatically adapted sheep breeds
columns.Description: Heat-adapted Turpan Black (n=15) versus cold-adapted Altay (n=15) sheep (Yang et al. 2026, *Foods*); integrates phenotypic meat-quality evaluation with non-targeted metabolomics and proteomics of longissimus dorsi to map how environmental adaptation shapes ovine meat quality; metabolome data openly deposited at FigShare (the deposit's title spans a third breed, Bayanbulak, beyond this paper's Turpan Black vs Altay comparison); the paper states no deposit location for the proteomics data

inventory.name: Comprehensive multi-tissue epigenome atlas in sheep: a resource for complex traits, domestication, and breeding

columns.Study: Comprehensive multi-tissue epigenome atlas in sheep: a resource for complex traits, domestication, and breeding
columns.Tissue: Nine major tissues (incl. longissimus dorsi, tail fat)
columns.Description: First multi-tissue epigenome atlas of sheep: 92 transcriptomic and epigenomic datasets across nine major tissues, cataloguing 753,723 nonredundant functional elements and their chromatin states; a regulatory-genomics reference for cultivated-lamb cell-line characterisation. Raw data at NGDC/GSA CRA019589 and [`CRA019576`](https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/gsa/search?searchTerm=CRA019576)

inventory.name: Satellite-cell clone heterogeneity during differentiation in turkey pectoralis major

columns.Study: Satellite-cell clone heterogeneity during differentiation in turkey pectoralis major
columns.Description: Transcriptomes of individual satellite-cell clones from one turkey p. major after 48 h differentiation, classed as early (fast-growing) vs late (slow-growing); >1,400 DEGs; MSTN upregulated in early clones, FGFBP1 in late (Yimiletey et al. 2025, *Poultry Science*)

inventory.name: Heterogeneity of satellite-cell populations from an individual turkey pectoralis major

columns.Study: Heterogeneity of satellite-cell populations from an individual turkey pectoralis major
columns.Description: RNA-seq of fast- vs slow-growing satellite-cell clones from the same p. major after 72 h proliferation; >5,300 DEGs; early clones enriched for muscle-development genes, late clones for ECM / niche / cytokine signaling (Yu et al. 2025, *Frontiers in Physiology*)

inventory.name: Transcriptome response of differentiating turkey satellite cells to thermal challenge

columns.Study: Transcriptome response of differentiating turkey satellite cells to thermal challenge
columns.Description: Satellite cells from fast-growing commercial (Nicholas, NCT) and slower research-line (Randombred Control Line 2, RBC2) turkeys proliferated at 38 °C then differentiated at 33/38/43 °C; RNA-seq DEGs isolate cold- and heat-stress responses in muscle regeneration and sarcomere organization (Reed et al. 2022, *Genes*)

inventory.name: Growth factor thermostability dataset (Ng et al.)

columns.Resource: Growth factor thermostability dataset (Ng et al.)
columns.Scope: 513 melting-temperature values across growth factors and variants used in cultured meat/seafood; 15-protein FoldX in silico subset

inventory.name: NMR metabolomics of plant and yeast-based hydrolysates (Combe et al.)

columns.Resource: NMR metabolomics of plant and yeast-based hydrolysates (Combe et al.)
columns.Scope: Comprehensive assessment of plant- and yeast-based hydrolysates intended as serum-free media components for cultivated meat; see paper's data availability statement for accession

inventory.name: Plant-based meat textural-properties training table (Kircali Ata et al.)

columns.Resource: Plant-based meat textural-properties training table (Kircali Ata et al.)
columns.Scope: Proximate composition (% protein/fat/carbohydrate/fibre/ash/moisture) + targeted moisture content → textural properties for plant-based meat analogs; training data for the Ridge / XGBoost / etc. regressors of [Papers.md #171](../Papers.md#171); no public repository accession

inventory.name: FR-AgENCODE multi-species farm-animal regulatory atlas (Foissac et al.)

columns.Resource: FR-AgENCODE multi-species farm-animal regulatory atlas (Foissac et al.)
columns.Scope: First FAANG multi-species, multi-assay genome annotation across cattle, goat, chicken, and pig (liver + CD4+/CD8+ T cells): extended transcript catalogs, differentially accessible chromatin, and Hi-C TADs / A/B compartments, with a conserved core of regulatory regions. ENA accessions PRJEB27455 (RNA-seq), PRJEB27111 (ATAC-seq), PRJEB27364 (Hi-C)

inventory.name: Comparative chromatin accessibility in cattle, pig, and mouse (Halstead et al.)

columns.Resource: Comparative chromatin accessibility in cattle, pig, and mouse (Halstead et al.)
columns.Scope: Consensus and tissue-specific open-chromatin maps across cattle, pig, and mouse tissues, with interspecies conservation assessed via the EPO whole-genome alignment. New cattle + pig ATAC-seq at ENA PRJEB14330; mouse ATAC-seq reused from CNGB CNP0000198

inventory.name: Mycelium mechanics & taste of fungi steak (Vervenne et al.)

columns.Resource: Mycelium mechanics & taste of fungi steak (Vervenne et al.)
columns.Scope: Fungal cell-ag texture reference: mechanical, rheological, and taste characterization of mycelium "fungi steak" as a whole-cut analog (its moist, fibrous signature), informing scaffold and texture targets reused across cultivated and fungal meats. Species-agnostic (fungal, not livestock); no sequencing deposit

inventory.name: Lion's mane mushroom-steak characterization (St. Pierre et al.)

columns.Resource: Lion's mane mushroom-steak characterization (St. Pierre et al.)
columns.Scope: Fungal cell-ag texture reference: mechanical, rheological, and sensory characterization of a lion's mane mushroom steak as a whole-cut analog, with texture/scaffold relevance across cultivated and fungal meats. bioRxiv preprint (not yet peer-reviewed); species-agnostic (fungal)
